newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar extends gains on low arrivals, stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar extends gains on low arrivals, stocks.

text.p: Sugar prices extended gains on the local market on Monday, as limited arrivals and shortage of ready stock dragged prices up despite slow demand from local consumers, dealers said.
"Fear that the Indian government may announce lower free sale quota for next month also triggered speculative interest in the market," one broker said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 5/10 rupees at 1,450/1,475 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 moved up by 5 rupees at 1,475/1,509 rupees per quintal.

Sugar mill delivery also climbed up to 1,395/1,410 rupees per quintal for the S-30 variety from 1,380/1,395 rupees while mill delivery for sugar M-30 rose to 1,415/1,435 rupees per quintal from 1,410/1,420 rupees.
Free sale quota for the current month is 800,000 tonnes and traders expected the government to announce a quota of 750,000 tonnes for next month.
Overall trading volume remained slow as major players kept to the sidelines awaiting the quota announcement but sentiment was firm at the close of the session.
